To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The radar waveform optimization problem can be formulated as a convex optimization problem, 2) The radar waveform design can be carried out in the time domain, 3) The radar waveform can be designed such that it maximizes the radar performance while strictly controlling the interference to the communication system, 4) A larger maximized Mutual information does not necessarily imply an optimal radar detection performance, 5) Exploiting the communication signals scattered from the target is important for radar detection performance,

(1) the maximized Mutual Information is not necessarily a good metric for radar waveform design; (2) the maximized radar detection performance does not necessarily guarantee the maximized Mutual information; and (3) exploiting the communication signals for the detection of weak radar targets can improve the detection performance.
A larger maximized Mutual Info. does not necessarily guarantee an optimal detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel radar waveform design methodology that exploits the available communication signals for the detection task.
the development of new waveform design techniques to improve the performance of joint radar and communication systems.
the design of radar waveforms that are robust to interference from communication signals and that are able to exploit the information contained in the scattered communication signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radar performance depends on the specific waveform optimization criterion and the radar scenario.
the proposed Mutual Information based criteria provide a good trade-off between radar performance and communication interference.
the Mutual Information based criteria should be used with care when designing the radar waveform, and the radar waveform optimization should be performed jointly with the radar target detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the radar waveform should be designed such that the radar performance is not degraded by the communication interference, and the communication performance should be improved by the radar interference.
A joint radar/communication
the radar should adapt its waveform to the communication signals scattered by the target, and not only the direct communication signals, in order to achieve an optimal radar performance.

the radar waveform design should be done in a way to minimize the interference to the communication systems, while the communication system design should be performed such that the radar performance is not degraded.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a joint radar and communication system, the design of the radar waveform should be based on a trade-off between maximizing the detection performance and minimizing the interference caused to cellular communication systems.
the radar waveform design should be based on the detection criterion of interest and the radar/communication system configuration.

the radar waveform optimization should be done with the consideration of the communication signals scattered from the target, and the maximization of the radar Mutual Information is not always the best choice.
